name: ps_end
prose: Finishes PostScript/PDF output for the mandoc terminal renderer. It first calls ps_plast (flush the pending last character) and ps_pclose (close an open text string). If PS_NEWPAGE is not set in p->ps->flags, meaning a page is still open, it asserts the flags and last-character state are clear and calls ps_closepage, which writes the pending page (margins, then showpage for PostScript, or the stream length, resource and page objects for PDF) and sets PS_NEWPAGE. For PostScript it then prints the %%Trailer, %%Pages count and %%EOF and returns. For PDF it writes the Pages node, the Catalog, the cross-reference table, trailer and %%EOF. All output goes through ps_printf, which writes to stdout (or into the growable margin buffer while PS_MARGINS is set) and updates pdfbytes; pdf_obj and ps_growbuf can reallocate the object table or the margin buffer, so the function can allocate memory. Returns nothing.
note: contrib/mandoc/term_ps.c:781-845 (closepage :730-778, pdf_obj :714-727). Reviewer (original) RIGHT: the final page is closed when PS_NEWPAGE is NOT set, i.e. when a page is open (:794). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: pdf_obj reallocates pdfobjs (:719-723) and ps_printf grows the margin buffer (:683).

name: ps_pclose
prose:
Closes an open text string in the PostScript/PDF renderer. If PS_INLINE is not set in p->ps->flags it returns immediately without output. Otherwise: for PDF output it prints ") Tj
ET
"; for PostScript, if the current row equals lastrow it prints ")c
", else it prints ")s
" and sets lastrow to the current row. Then it clears PS_INLINE. Returns nothing.
note: contrib/mandoc/term_ps.c:1037-1059. Reviewer (original) RIGHT: the inline check, the two output forms and the lastrow update were missing. Reviewer (r15) WRONG: the code does clear PS_INLINE at :1058.

name: GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(fore)
prose: Generated function int set_field_fore(FIELD *field, chtype attr) (macro GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(fore), documented as setting the field's foreground attribute). It starts with the result E_BAD_ARGUMENT. If attr is A_NORMAL or consists only of attribute bits (attr & A_ATTRIBUTES) == attr, it replaces a NULL field argument by the default field (Normalize_Field), so a NULL field modifies the default field instead of failing; then if the stored fore attribute differs from attr it stores attr and returns _nc_Synchronize_Attributes(field), which can return E_OK, E_BAD_ARGUMENT or the result of Display_Field (for example E_SYSTEM_ERROR); if the stored value already equals attr it returns E_OK without synchronising. For an attr containing non-attribute bits nothing is changed and E_BAD_ARGUMENT is returned.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/fld_attr.c:42-64 (macro), invocation :85; Normalize_Field at contrib/ncurses/form/form.priv.h:99-100; _nc_Synchronize_Attributes at contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:1279-1328. Reviewers RIGHT: E_SYSTEM_ERROR can come from the synchronisation (original); a NULL field is normalised to the default field (r15).

name: GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(back)
prose: Generated function int set_field_back(FIELD *field, chtype attr) (macro GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(back), documented as setting the field's background attribute). It starts with the result E_BAD_ARGUMENT. If attr is A_NORMAL or consists only of attribute bits (attr & A_ATTRIBUTES) == attr, it replaces a NULL field argument by the default field (Normalize_Field), so a NULL field modifies the default field instead of failing; then if the stored back attribute differs from attr it stores attr and returns _nc_Synchronize_Attributes(field), which can return E_OK, E_BAD_ARGUMENT or the result of Display_Field (for example E_SYSTEM_ERROR); if the stored value already equals attr it returns E_OK without synchronising. For an attr containing non-attribute bits nothing is changed and E_BAD_ARGUMENT is returned.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/fld_attr.c:42-64 (macro), invocation :108; Normalize_Field at contrib/ncurses/form/form.priv.h:99-100; _nc_Synchronize_Attributes at contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:1279-1328. Reviewers RIGHT: E_SYSTEM_ERROR can come from the synchronisation (original); a NULL field is normalised to the default field (r15).

name: set_current_field
prose: Public libnform call that makes `field` the current field of `form`. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT if form or field is NULL; E_REQUEST_DENIED if the field belongs to another form or is not selectable. If the form is not posted it just stores the field as current and sets curpage from the field's page, and returns E_OK without hooks. If posted: E_BAD_STATE while the driver is running (_IN_DRIVER); if the field is already current nothing happens and the result is E_OK; otherwise it validates the current field with _nc_Internal_Validation (failure gives E_INVALID_FIELD and no change), then calls the field-term hook, moves to the new field either through _nc_Set_Form_Page (when the page differs, with the form-term and form-init hooks around it) or _nc_Set_Current_Field, calls the field-init hook and refreshes the current field, returning the error code of the move; hooks and the refresh run even if the move reported an error, and a failed move can leave the form's current field or window changed.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/fld_current.c:52-104. Reviewers RIGHT: errors from _nc_Set_Form_Page/_nc_Set_Current_Field do not guarantee 'no change' (original); hooks/refresh are skipped when unposted or when the field is already current (r15).

name: _nc_Set_Current_Field
prose: Makes `newfield` the current field of `form`, creating the field's display window. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT if form or newfield is NULL or newfield belongs to another form; E_BAD_STATE if the driver is running; E_NOT_CONNECTED if the form has no fields. If newfield is already current and the form is posted it skips the window work and goes straight to the final step, so E_OK can be returned without creating a new window. Otherwise: if there is a current field with a window that is visible and on the current page it calls _nc_Unset_Current_Field on it; it then creates a new pad (field with invisible parts) or a derived window for the field, returning E_SYSTEM_ERROR if that fails (at that point the previous current field has already been unset but form->current and form->w are unchanged); on success it sets form->current, deletes the old form->w, installs the new window, clears _WINDOW_MODIFIED, applies the field's window attributes and redraws buffer contents. In all successful paths it sets currow, curcol, toprow and begincol to 0 and returns E_OK.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:1499-1565. Reviewers RIGHT: E_OK can occur without creating a new window when newfield is already current and the form is posted (round 2, :1517-1518).

name: IFN_Next_Word
prose: Intra-field navigation: moves the cursor to the start of the next word in the current field. It synchronises the buffer itself (Synchronize_Buffer), so the caller need not. It finds the first whitespace after the cursor position and then the start of data after it, and moves the cursor there with Adjust_Cursor_Position, returning E_OK. In this build FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD is defined as 1, so when there is no next word (the two positions coincide) it still returns E_OK and the cursor is moved to the position found, which is the end of the data, not the start of a word; the E_REQUEST_DENIED return exists only when FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD is 0.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:1703-1733; FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD defined at contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:96. Reviewers RIGHT: function synchronises the buffer itself (:1713) (original); no-next-word path returns E_OK at the end of data (r15).

name: IFN_Previous_Word
prose: Intra-field navigation: moves the cursor to the start of the previous word in the current field. It synchronises the buffer itself. It finds the end of data before the cursor (After_End_Of_Data); if the cursor was inside a word (that position equals the cursor) it repeats the search once more from before that word's start; it then finds the position after the last whitespace before it and moves the cursor there with Adjust_Cursor_Position, returning E_OK. With FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD defined as 1 (as in this file) a missing previous word does not yield E_REQUEST_DENIED: the function still returns E_OK, with the cursor moved to the position found (the start of the buffer region examined) rather than to a real previous word.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:1745-1787. Reviewers RIGHT: buffer synchronised internally (:1756) (original); with FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD the no-previous-word case returns E_OK (:1771-1783 are compiled out) (r15).

name: FE_New_Line
prose: Field-editing request for a new line in the current field. Let Last_Row be true when the cursor is on the field's last data row. Overlay mode (_OVLMODE): if Last_Row and the field is not growable-and-multi-line, it returns E_REQUEST_DENIED unless the form has O_NL_OVERLOAD, in which case it clears to end of line, sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED and returns the result of Inter_Field_Navigation(FN_Next_Field). Otherwise (not last row, or a growable multi-line field) it grows the field by one row first when on the last row (E_SYSTEM_ERROR if that fails), clears to end of line, increments currow, sets curcol = 0, sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED and returns E_OK. Insert mode: if Last_Row and not growable-multi-line it returns E_REQUEST_DENIED without O_NL_OVERLOAD, else the Inter_Field_Navigation result; otherwise it needs room for a line or a growable field (E_REQUEST_DENIED if neither; E_SYSTEM_ERROR if growing fails) and splits the line at the cursor: clears to end of line, moves to the next row at column 0, inserts a line and writes the rest of the old line there, sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED and returns E_OK. So the Inter_Field_Navigation result is returned only on the overload path, and a last-row growable multi-line field grows instead of navigating.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:2634-2707. Reviewers RIGHT: the overload path returns the Inter_Field_Navigation result, not E_OK with currow advanced (original); growable multi-line fields grow instead of navigating (:2643-2644, :2657-2672) (r15).

name: FE_Insert_Character
prose: Field-editing request that inserts a blank at the cursor. It starts with E_REQUEST_DENIED and proceeds only if Check_Char accepts a blank (C_BLANK) for the field's type; if it does not accept it, E_REQUEST_DENIED is returned with no change. If there is room in the line, or the field is single-line and growable, it grows the field when there is no room (E_SYSTEM_ERROR if growing fails) and otherwise inserts the blank with winsch and returns the result of Wrapping_Not_Necessary_Or_Wrapping_Ok, which may be E_OK or an error such as E_REQUEST_DENIED or E_SYSTEM_ERROR; when wrapping fails the inserted character has been put into the window and is then deleted again, so the window is modified and restored rather than untouched. If there is no room and the field is not growable single-line, it returns E_REQUEST_DENIED.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:2719-2743; Wrapping_Not_Necessary_Or_Wrapping_Ok in the same file (read to its DeleteChar undo path). Reviewers RIGHT: E_REQUEST_DENIED can follow the winsch (original); Check_Char rejection is handled (:2725-2741) (r15).

name: _nc_Internal_Validation
prose: Validates the current field of `form`; returns TRUE (non-zero) if the field is accepted or needs no check, FALSE if the field-type check rejects the contents. It first calls Synchronize_Buffer(form). It checks the field only if the form has _FCHECK_REQUIRED set or the field does not have the O_PASSOK option: then Check_Field must succeed (otherwise it returns FALSE with no further change); on success it clears _FCHECK_REQUIRED on the form, sets _CHANGED on the field and synchronises linked fields. When O_PASSOK is set and _FCHECK_REQUIRED is not, it skips the check and these updates and returns TRUE. A current field must exist (form->current is dereferenced).
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:3237-3254. Reviewers RIGHT: Synchronize_Buffer is called (original); updates are skipped for O_PASSOK without _FCHECK_REQUIRED (:3244-3252), and a failed Check_Field returns FALSE (r15).

name: Data_Entry
prose: Handles the typing of one character c into the current field of `form`. Returns E_REQUEST_DENIED unless the field has O_EDIT (and O_ACTIVE when FIX_FORM_INACTIVE_BUG is built); the window and buffer are then untouched. If the field has O_BLANK, the cursor is at the first position and neither _FCHECK_REQUIRED nor _WINDOW_MODIFIED is set, the window is erased. In overlay mode it writes the character with waddch; in insert mode it requires room in the line or a growable single-line field (else E_REQUEST_DENIED), grows the field if needed (E_SYSTEM_ERROR on failure) and inserts with winsch. It then calls Wrapping_Not_Necessary_Or_Wrapping_Ok; only if that returns E_OK it records whether the cursor is at the field's end (and sets move_after_insert for O_EDGE_INSERT_STAY), sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED, and: if at the end of a non-growable field with O_AUTOSKIP it returns the result of Inter_Field_Navigation(FN_Next_Field); else if at the end of a growable field and growing fails it returns E_SYSTEM_ERROR; else it moves to the next character position (unless a multibyte character is still incomplete) and returns E_OK. If wrapping returns an error, that error is returned and _WINDOW_MODIFIED is not set.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:4159-4234. Reviewers RIGHT: non-editable field gives E_REQUEST_DENIED (original), and _WINDOW_MODIFIED is set only after E_OK from the wrapping check (:4196-4207) (round 2).

name: form_driver
prose: Public libnform driver: processes request or character c for form. It first sets the file-level move_after_insert to TRUE. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT for a NULL form and E_NOT_CONNECTED when the form has no fields or no current field (both checked before any other work). The special value FIRST_ACTIVE_MAGIC sets form->current to the first active field and returns E_OK. Then E_BAD_STATE if the driver is running and E_NOT_POSTED if the form is not posted. If c is a form command whose binding matches, the command's generic method (page, field, scrolling or editing wrapper, or none) is run, giving E_SYSTEM_ERROR when the method index is out of range or the command function is missing; otherwise the command's result. With mouse support, KEY_MOUSE events are mapped to field/page requests or selection of a field under the click (E_REQUEST_DENIED when the click is not usable). For a regular character, if it is printable (and, in the non-wide build, accepted by Check_Char) it calls Data_Entry; otherwise the result stays E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND. After all paths that reach the end it calls _nc_Refresh_Current_Field and returns the result.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_driver.c:4366-4538 (early returns :4376, :4379, :4386, :4395, :4398; final refresh :4536). Reviewer (original) RIGHT: E_SYSTEM_ERROR for an invalid method or missing command (:4425-4426). Reviewer (r15) WRONG: the function does set move_after_insert = TRUE (:4371) and does return E_NOT_CONNECTED when there is no current field (:4378).

name: set_form_sub
prose: Sets the subwindow used to display a form. If form is non-NULL and posted it returns E_POSTED without change. Otherwise Normalize_Form replaces a NULL form argument by the default form (so the default form is modified), and the subwindow is set: in builds with NCURSES_SP_FUNCS, form->sub = win if win is non-NULL, else the screen's standard window; in builds without it, form->sub = win, which may be NULL. Returns E_OK in both builds.
note: contrib/ncurses/form/frm_sub.c:47-65. Reviewer (original) RIGHT: non-SP build stores NULL for win == NULL (:61). Reviewer (r15) WRONG: Normalize_Form(form) assigns the local parameter (form.priv.h:95-96), so the SP branch dereferences the normalised form (:57-58).

name: post_menu
prose: Posts a menu. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT for NULL, E_BAD_STATE if the menu driver is running (_IN_DRIVER), E_POSTED if already posted, and E_NOT_CONNECTED if the menu has no items. Otherwise it creates a pad menu->win sized for the menu and a subpad menu->sub; if newpad fails it returns E_SYSTEM_ERROR, and if subpad fails it also returns E_SYSTEM_ERROR but leaves menu->win allocated (menu->sub is NULL), so the menu is changed. Then it relinks items if _LINK_NEEDED, sets _POSTED, clears each item's value when O_ONEVALUE is not set, draws the menu, calls the menu-init and item-init hooks, shows the menu and returns E_OK.
note: contrib/ncurses/menu/m_post.c:277-335 (return sites :282, :285, :288, :304, :307, :313, :334). Reviewers RIGHT: subpad failure leaves menu->win allocated (:297-305) (original); _IN_DRIVER and _POSTED states are handled with E_BAD_STATE and E_POSTED (r15).

name: waddch_literal
prose: Stores one literal character cell at the window cursor (the wide-character build is described). It applies CHECK_POSITION, renders the character with the window's background (render_char) and marks the cell changed. If an incomplete multibyte sequence is pending or the character is not a single byte, _nc_build_wch assembles it: a complete character replaces ch; if the sequence is still incomplete the function returns OK without storing anything; on an encoding error (len == -1) an 8-bit character whose unctrl form is longer than one character is output as that expansion through waddch (returning the first failure), otherwise it returns waddch(win, ' ' | attr). Then by display width: width 0 (non-spacing) is added to the previous cell's character list (the previous line's last cell at column 0), no new cell is written and the cursor stays; width greater than 1: if wider than the window it returns ERR, if it does not fit on the line the rest of the line is blank-filled and the cursor wraps (ERR if wrapping fails), orphaned cells are blanked, and the width cells are written; width 1: the cell is stored and x advances. Finally if x is past the last column it returns wrap_to_next_line(win), else it sets the cursor column and returns OK.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/base/lib_addch.c:257-431 (wide-character code at :282-312, :320-409); _nc_build_wch :189-249. Reviewers RIGHT: non-spacing characters merge into the previous cell and incomplete multibyte input returns OK without storing (original); the EILSEQ fallback waddch(win, ' ' | attr) (:306-307) is part of the behaviour (r15).

name: _nc_background
prose: Common implementation of wbkgd (narrow) and wbkgrnd (wide) background setting for window win with background character ch. It returns ERR if the screen (SP) is NULL or win is NULL. Otherwise it forms the new background (colour info is dropped on a terminal without colour pairs, a null character becomes a blank with the same attributes). If the new background is identical to the current one it returns OK at once without changing anything. Otherwise it sets the window background (wbkgrndset), sets the window attributes (and the colour pair when the old and new pair are equal and non-zero), then visits every cell of the window: cells whose character equals the old background character get the new background character; every cell's attributes and colour pair are recomputed (old background attributes removed, new ones added, depending on its colour pair), not only the cells that matched the old background; finally it touches the whole window, calls _nc_synchook and returns OK. In the narrow call a non-charable new background keeps the old character.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/base/lib_bkgd.c:118-257 (unchanged return :171; cell loop :214-251). Reviewers RIGHT: unchanged background returns OK without remapping (original); attribute remapping covers every cell (r15).

name: endwin
prose: Ends curses mode for the screen and restores the shell terminal mode. In builds with NCURSES_SP_FUNCS the public endwin() simply returns the screen-pointer version called with CURRENT_SCREEN (lines 79-83); the logic described here is in lines 48-76 (in other builds this is endwin itself). The result starts as ERR. If the screen pointer is non-NULL: when the screen is not already in the suspended state it sets the suspended state, runs the terminal-driver or mouse/screen/mvcur wrap-up and sets the result to OK; then, whether or not it was already suspended, it calls reset_shell_mode, and if that returns ERR the result becomes ERR. So the result is OK only when this call performed the suspend and reset_shell_mode succeeded; a NULL screen, a second endwin without refresh, or a reset_shell_mode failure gives ERR.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/base/lib_endwin.c:48-84. Reviewers RIGHT: a NULL current screen is handled and returns ERR (original); result is not just 0/-1 but follows the conditions above (r15). Second call while already suspended returns ERR (code only set to OK inside the not-suspended branch, :56-70).

name: fifo_push
prose: Reads one more input key and appends it to the screen's key fifo; returns the key stored, ERR, or KEY_EVENT. Static helper in lib_getch.c, with several configuration-dependent branches. It returns ERR immediately if tail < 0 (the fifo has no room, nothing is stored). With event support, if an event list is given (or a mouse fd exists) it checks mouse/event activity; an event result makes it ungetch KEY_EVENT and return KEY_EVENT without storing to the fifo. A pending GPM or sysmouse (or terminal-driver mouse) event is handled by calling the mouse-event routine and the key becomes KEY_MOUSE. Otherwise it blocks reading one byte from the input (through the driver, console read or read()), and a read result of -1 or 0 makes the key ERR. It then stores the key at sp->_fifo[tail], clears _fifohold, sets head and peek to tail when the fifo was empty (head == -1), advances tail with t_inc and returns the key; this storing path is the same for mouse keys and ERR, so ERR is also pushed in that case.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/base/lib_getch.c:224-343 (function head at :224). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the mouse branch also clears _fifohold, initialises head/peek and advances the tail (:330-334). Partly read: t_inc, check_mouse_activity, safe_ungetch not read.

name: allow_gpm_mouse
prose: Decides whether ncurses may use the GPM mouse library (compiled only with USE_GPM_SUPPORT); returns bool, starting from FALSE. With weak-symbol support, if the GPM function Gpm_Wgetch is already linked in or loaded, it skips the remaining checks and returns FALSE (it reads sp->_mouse_gpm_loaded only to trace whether ncurses loaded it). Otherwise, if stdout is a terminal: when the environment variable NCURSES_GPM_TERMS is set the result is TRUE only if TERM is set and matches that list (_nc_name_match with separators "|:"); when it is not set the result is TRUE only if TERM is set and contains "linux". If stdout is not a terminal it returns FALSE. It only reads the environment and sp; nothing else is modified.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/base/lib_mouse.c:469-503. Reviewers RIGHT: skip stdout/env checks and return FALSE when GPM is already loaded (original); sp is dereferenced in the weak-symbol branch (:476) although declared GCC_UNUSED (r15).

name: NCURSES_SP_NAME(resize_term)
prose: Resizes the terminal model of `sp` to ToLines x ToCols. Returns ERR at once, before taking the lock, if sp is NULL or either size is not positive. Otherwise it locks the global curses lock and computes the number of stolen (ripped-off) lines; only if is_term_resized reports that the size differs does it resize windows: it increases line count first (increase_size), then column count, then decreases if either target is smaller (decrease_size), each stopping with ERR if a window adjustment fails. If all succeeded, in that branch it updates the stored screen size (and the terminal driver's size or the lines/columns variables), sets _lines_avail, and frees and clears the old and new hash arrays (oldhash and newhash). If the size is unchanged it does none of this and the hash arrays stay allocated. Whenever the result is OK, including the unchanged case, it also updates LINES and COLS (minus stolen lines), then unlocks and returns the result (OK or ERR).
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/base/resizeterm.c:351-448 (early return :361-363; lock :365; unlock :445). Reviewers RIGHT: early invalid-argument return is before the lock (original); hash arrays are freed only in the changed-size branch (:406-424) (round 2).

name: resize_term
prose: Public resize_term(ToLines, ToCols) in builds with NCURSES_SP_FUNCS: takes the global curses lock (_nc_sp_lock_global), calls the screen-pointer version with CURRENT_SCREEN and the same sizes, releases the lock and returns the result. So the argument and NULL-screen checks are made inside that callee (ERR), after this wrapper has locked.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/base/resizeterm.c:451-459. Reviewer comments about hash arrays and early return apply to the callee at :351-448, not to this wrapper.

name: _nc_merge_entry
prose: Merges the capabilities of source entry into target entry (both ENTRY structures); returns void. It returns immediately if source, target or their term types are NULL. With extended names (NCURSES_XNAMES) it copies the source term type, aligns the extended capability tables of target and the copy, and rebuilds both string tables: all names and string capabilities of the copy and of the target are copied into one newly malloc'ed table (the program aborts through _nc_err_abort when malloc fails), the target's pointers are repointed into it and the old target table and the copy's table are freed; the extended-name strings get the same treatment. Then, for each source capability within the target's counts: booleans: if the target value is not CANCELLED, a source CANCELLED sets it FALSE, a source TRUE sets it TRUE, and a source FALSE or ABSENT leaves it unchanged; numbers: if the target is not CANCELLED, a source CANCELLED makes it ABSENT, a source that is not ABSENT replaces it, and ABSENT leaves it; strings: the same rule with CANCELLED_STRING/ABSENT_STRING (a present source string replaces the target string, pointing into the new table). The temporary copy arrays are freed at the end.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/tinfo/alloc_entry.c:249-412 (function head :249). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: a source FALSE boolean leaves the target unchanged (:362-372). Partly read: _nc_copy_termtype2, _nc_align_termtype.

name: _nc_get_token
prose: Terminfo/termcap lexer: reads the next token from the input set up by the compiler and returns its type (NAMES, BOOLEAN, CANCEL, NUMBER, STRING, EOF or UNDEF), filling _nc_curr_token. If a token was pushed back it restores it (_nc_set_type with the pushed name), clears the pushback and returns its type. If the stream is at its end it returns EOF and clears tk_name if that pointed at tok_buf. Otherwise it skips blanks and newlines (tracking a newline for the termcap warning), handles an optional leading '.' (commented-out entry: it parses the token and then returns the result of a recursive call for the next one), and skips illegal leading characters through _nc_panic_mode, warning unless silent. At the start of an entry line it reads the name field up to the separator, deciding between termcap (':') and terminfo (',') syntax; running out of input inside that name line calls _nc_err_abort(MSG_NO_INPUTS) and does not return. It sets tk_name to tok_buf and returns NAMES. Elsewhere it reads an identifier and then by the next character: ',' or ':' returns BOOLEAN (a separator that does not match the syntax calls _nc_err_abort 'Separator inconsistent with syntax'); '@' returns CANCEL; '#' reads digits into a number buffer, returns NUMBER with tk_valnumber, and when not silent warns on missing, negative or oversized values and clamps the value to the NCURSES_INT2 maximum; '=' translates the string with _nc_trans_string and returns STRING with tk_valstring; end of input or a full buffer gives EOF; any other character gives UNDEF with a warning when not silent. Warnings do not change the return value.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/tinfo/comp_scan.c:386-817 (head at :386; packet slice 542-795 is the middle; first-column name parse :498-666, other tokens :666-752). Reviewer (r17) WRONG: end of input inside the first-column name line calls _nc_err_abort (:507-508), it does not return NAMES. Earlier prose said number clamping happens only when not silent: confirmed (:715-727). Real function name _nc_get_token; packet name tic_token_parser does not exist.

name: _nc_timed_wait
prose: Waits for input, mouse or event activity on the screen's file descriptors for up to `milliseconds` (negative means no timeout); mode is a bitmask (TW_INPUT, TW_MOUSE, TW_EVENT); returns a bitmask of the ready sources, 0 on timeout, error or interruption, or TW_NONE if the poll descriptor array cannot be allocated in an event build. With events, a pending event timeout shorter than the requested wait replaces it. It records a start time, then uses poll (descriptors for the input fd, the mouse fd and readable event files), or a BeOS loop, or select, to wait; event results are recorded in the event list. It then reduces `milliseconds` by the elapsed time and decrements event timeouts, and with PRECISE_GETTIME and nanosleep, if nothing happened and more than 100 ms remain, it sleeps 100 ms and repeats the wait. If timeleft is non-NULL it stores the remaining milliseconds in *timeleft. A positive poll/select result is turned into the bits for the ready descriptors (poll: the bit position is the slot index for each of the first MIN_FDS slots with POLLIN set and the bit present in mode; select: TW_MOUSE and TW_INPUT by FD_ISSET), a zero or negative result becomes 0, and the TW_EVENT bit is added when the event list reports activity. A malloc'ed poll array is freed before returning.

name: TransformLine
prose: Updates terminal line `lineno` from the new screen image (newLine) to the current screen image (oldLine) with as little output as possible; returns void. It first copies the new line's hash into the old hash. With colour, cells that differ only in colour pair number but whose pairs are the same colours get the new pair number in oldLine. If the terminal has ceol_standout_glitch and clr_eol and any cell's attributes changed, it moves to column 0, clears to end of line and rewrites the whole line. Else, if magic_cookie_glitch > 0 (USE_XMC_SUPPORT) it writes the line cell by cell with PutChar, skipping cells that would hold cookies. Otherwise it finds the first differing cell (optionally using clr_bol for leading blanks) and returns without output if there is none; when the last cell cannot be cleared with a blank it writes the range of differing cells and copies it into oldLine before returning; otherwise it compares the last non-blank cells and chooses between clearing to end of line, rewriting a range, inserting characters (InsStr) or deleting characters (DelChar), using the cost estimates. After the chain of cases (including the attribute-change and magic-cookie cases) it copies newLine[firstChar..] into oldLine, so oldLine matches newLine afterwards in those branches too.

Reviewers (original and r15) WRONG: the magic-cookie branch is an `else if` of the same chain, and the memcpy at :1633-1636 after the chain runs for it too (firstChar is 0 there), so oldLine is updated. Partly read: PutRange, ClrToEOL, InsStr and DelChar internals.

name: _nc_is_charable
prose: Reports whether the wide character ch is a single-byte character in the current locale whose byte value equals the code point. With wctob available it returns wctob((wint_t) ch) == (int) ch, which is true only when wctob maps ch to the same value (for example ASCII, or Latin-1 in a Latin-1 locale) and false when ch is not a single byte (wctob returns EOF) or maps to a different byte value; without wctob it returns _nc_to_char(ch) >= 0, i.e. whenever ch converts to some single byte. It has no side effects beyond the locale's conversion state.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/widechar/charable.c:38-47. Reviewer (round 2) RIGHT: the wctob build requires wctob(ch) == ch, so a single-byte character whose byte value differs from ch is not charable.

name: _nc_to_char
prose: Converts the wide character ch to a single byte of the current locale and returns it as an int in 0..255, or a negative value when it is not representable as one byte. With wctob it returns wctob(ch) (EOF, normally -1, when ch has no single-byte form). Without wctob it calls wctomb into a local buffer and returns the unsigned first byte if exactly one byte was produced, else -1. No other state changes except the multibyte conversion state.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/widechar/charable.c:49-64. Reviewers RIGHT: result is tied to the locale encoding, not only to ch > 127 (round 1/2).

name: NCURSES_SP_NAME(term_attrs)
prose: Returns the highlight attributes supported by the terminal as a wide attr_t mask. If the screen pointer is NULL it returns 0. Otherwise it starts from termattrs() for that screen and, in wide-character builds where the terminfo has the horizontal-highlight capabilities, ORs in WA_HORIZONTAL, WA_LEFT, WA_LOW, WA_RIGHT, WA_TOP and WA_VERTICAL for each corresponding enter_*_hl_mode capability that is set. The public term_attrs() (SP builds) calls this with CURRENT_SCREEN. Reads terminal capabilities only.
note: contrib/ncurses/ncurses/widechar/lib_vid_attr.c:335-361; wrapper :365-368.

name: show_entry
prose: Writes the accumulated terminfo/termcap entry text outbuf to stdout and returns the number of characters in outbuf.used afterwards. If outbuf.used != 0 it trims the end first: scanning backwards from the last character (index > 0), a newline is skipped without trimming, a whitespace character truncates the buffer to that index (removing it), in termcap mode a backslash also truncates to that index, and a delimiter (',' for terminfo, ':' for termcap) not preceded by a backslash sets the length to just after it; any other character stops the scan. The scan continues after the delimiter case, so whitespace before a delimiter can be removed together with the delimiter. It then NUL-terminates at outbuf.used (outbuf.text is dereferenced, so it must be non-NULL when used != 0). Finally, if outbuf.text is non-NULL it prints it followed by a newline. A trailing newline preceded by a non-space character is not removed.
note: contrib/ncurses/progs/dump_entry.c:1680-1711. Reviewers RIGHT: trailing newline can remain (round 1), scan can trim whitespace before a delimiter (round 2), text must be non-NULL when used != 0 (r15).

name: decode_tabs
prose: Parses a tab-stop specification such as "1,10,16,36,72" or "+8" into a newly allocated int array terminated by 0, or returns NULL. It allocates strlen(tab_list) + max_cols ints (failed() on allocation failure) and treats a negative margin as 0. For each character: a digit accumulates a value (limited to max_cols); ',' stores value + prior + margin as the next stop, and if this stop is not greater than the previous stop it prints 'tab-stops are not in increasing order', frees the array and returns NULL; '+' sets prior to the previous stop (if there is one) so the next number is relative; other characters are ignored. After the loop, if there was only a single number (no comma) it is treated as a step: stops 1+margin, 1+margin+step, ... are generated for up to max_cols - 1 entries. Finally the last value (value + prior + margin) is appended and a 0 terminator is stored; this final value is not checked against the previous stop's order. Stops generated or appended are not clamped to max_cols beyond the per-number limit on the digits.
note: contrib/ncurses/progs/tabs.c:123-183. Reviewers RIGHT: negative margin clamped to 0 (round 2, :134-135); the final appended stop is not order-checked and generated stops are not clamped (round 1, :166-178).

name: main
prose: Entry point of the tabs utility. It takes the terminal name from -T or $TERM (default "ansi+tabs") and parses options: predefined tab lists (-a, -a2, -c, -c2, -c3, -f, -p, -s, -u), -d (debug), -n (no operation), -V (print version and exit successfully), a numeric list, +mN margin and further tab-list words (collected with add_to_tab_list); an unknown option calls usage(). It saves the tty settings, calls setupterm, sets max_cols from the terminal width (80 if none) minus the margin, and then: if the terminal has no clear_all_tabs it prints 'cannot reset tabs'; else if it has no set_tab it prints 'cannot set tabs'; else if the list is legal it defaults to "8" when no list was given and, unless -n was given, switches off OCRNL when stdout is a tty (changing the tty settings), and clears the old tabs; it sets the margin when requested, decodes the list with decode_tabs, and if the list decoded it sets the tab stops with do_tabs unless -n was given and prints a ruler and tab list when -d was given; with -n it does not clear or set tabs and does not change or restore the tty settings; it restores the tty if it changed it, and exits with EXIT_SUCCESS in that branch (even when decode_tabs returned NULL and only an error message was printed). In the 'cannot reset/set tabs' or illegal-list cases the exit status is EXIT_FAILURE.
note: contrib/ncurses/progs/tabs.c:479-710 (head at :479; slice 557-710 is the tail). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: no_op (-n) skips clearing/setting tabs and tty restore (:654-669, :687-704). Partly read: legal_tab_list, add_to_tab_list, do_set_margin.

prose: ATF test body for reading the kernfs root directory. It calls mountkernfs() (rump_init, mkdir /kern, mount kernfs; any failure fails the test), opens /kern read-only and calls getdents into an 8192-byte buffer, failing the test on an error from either call. It then requires (ATF_REQUIRE_STREQ, fatal) that the first three directory entries are named ".", ".." and "boottime" in that order. The directory descriptor is not closed.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(hostname, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking that /kern/hostname reflects and changes the system hostname. It mounts kernfs and opens /kern/hostname read-write; it reads the file (failing the test on error), cuts it at the first newline, and requires it to equal the hostname obtained through sysctl(KERN_HOSTNAME). It then writes "turboton roos-berg" at offset 0 with pwrite (failing unless all bytes are written) and requires the sysctl hostname to equal that string. The read buffer is not NUL-terminated after the read, so the first-newline search relies on the file content ending with a newline; the descriptor is not closed.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(utypefit, tc)
prose: ATF test body (function utypefit_body) that checks the __type_fit macro for unsigned types with fatal ATF_REQUIRE checks. For unsigned char, short, int and long long it requires __type_fit to be 0 for -1, 1 for 1, 1 for the values up to the type's maximum (0x7f, 0x80, 0xff for char, 0x7fff-0xffff for short, 0x7fffffff-0xffffffff for int, 0x7fff...-0xffff... for long long) and 0 for a value that needs more bits: 0x1ff for char, 0x1ffff for short, 0x1ffffffffLL for int (not the maximum plus one); there is no overflow case for unsigned long long. Returns nothing; a failed check ends the test.
